lines: Pick a style and watch its phrase. Turn on Trace to see the shape it leaves in space.
Two styles, one clock. Press Play, then turn on Overlay to lay one trace over the other.
Press Note when you see something worth saying. It's stamped to that count.
Each ghost is half a count apart. Hands draw solid lines, feet draw dotted ones.
Tall bars are strong accents. Dots are the sound of the feet.
Now tap Insert note under a box, so every claim points to a moment.
Ballet began in Renaissance courts and grew up in France, which is why its words are French.
Modern dance broke ballet's rules and let weight, breath and the floor back in.
Jazz dance grew from African American social dance into theater and film.
In tap, the dancer is also the drummer. Listen as much as you watch.
Breaking started at Bronx block parties in the 1970s, danced to the breaks of records.
Irish step dance keeps the arms still, so all the speed lives in the feet.
Flamenco joins song, guitar and dance in a cycle of twelve counts.
Bharatanatyam, from South India, tells stories with the hands and keeps time with the feet.
